did_you_know.text: The phrase “grown old in days” is a common biblical idiom meaning advanced age and is often used to introduce a farewell speech.
The term “Book of the Law of Moses” refers to the collection of laws attributed to Moses, and the formula “do not turn right or left” is a biblical way to stress strict obedience.
The saying “one man of you shall chase a thousand” is a literary exaggeration meant to stress that military victories came from the LORD’s help, not merely from troop numbers.
The claim “not one word has failed” expresses the belief that God’s promises were fully realized — a biblical formula used to explain Israel’s early success in settling the land.

The idea that covenant breach and foreign worship bring swift destruction is a central motif in the Deuteronomistic reading of biblical history: blessing for obedience, punishment for breaking the covenant.
